title_en: Ma Ping's Application for State Compensation
ruling_gist_en: The public security authority, in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, recovered the high-interest portion paid by the criminal suspect to the compensation claimant in this case from the proceeds of the bill fraud crime and returned it to the defrauded bank. Its conduct was not improper and has been confirmed by the effective criminal judgment of the people's court, therefore it does not fall under the circumstances specified in Article 18(1) of the State Compensation Law of the PRC. The compensation claimant's act of receiving high-interest was unlawful and did not meet the requirements for bona fide acquisition under Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Fraud Cases.

full_text_en:
Ma Ping v. Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau — State Compensation Case

【Ruling Summary】

Where a public security authority, in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, recovers the portion of high interest paid to the compensation claimant in this case from the proceeds of a crime of bill fraud by a criminal suspect and returns it to the defrauded bank, such conduct is not improper and has been confirmed by a legally effective criminal judgment of a People's Court. Therefore, it does not fall under the circumstances stipulated in Article 18(1) of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China. The compensation claimant's act of receiving high interest is illegal and does not satisfy the circumstances of bona fide acquisition as provided in Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Fraud Cases.

Supreme People's Court
Compensation Committee
State Compensation Decision

(2012) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 4

Compensation Claimant: Ma Ping, female, Han nationality, born January 11, 1958, Australian citizen, currently residing at Room 301, Unit 5, Building 2, Julong Garden, No. 68 Xinzhong Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Agent ad litem: Chang Junfeng, lawyer from Beijing King & Wood Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Sun Guangzhi, lawyer from Beijing King & Wood Law Firm.

Compensation Obligor: Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, domiciled at No. 26 Tangshan Road, Heping District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Wu Changshun, Director of Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiaoyi, cadre of the Economic Crime Investigation General Team of Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yi, cadre of the Legal Affairs Office of Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau.

Compensation Review Authority: Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China, domiciled at No. 14 East Chang'an Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Guo Shengkun, Minister of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Wei Di, cadre of the Legal Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yong, cadre of the Legal Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China.

The compensation claimant, Ma Ping, dissatisfied with the criminal compensation review decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi (2012) No. 2) issued by the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Ministry of Public Security) on April 19, 2012, regarding the application for state compensation from the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau for unlawful recovery in a criminal case, has applied to the Compensation Committee of this Court for a compensation decision. The Compensation Committee of this Court has conducted a trial by examination of evidence in this case and now concludes the trial.

Ma Ping requests from the Compensation Committee of this Court: to revoke the criminal compensation review decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi (2012) No. 2) of the Ministry of Public Security and the criminal compensation decision (Jin Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 001) of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau; to determine that the act of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau in recovering RMB 12.72 million from her was illegal; and to compensate her for RMB 12.72 million and interest losses of RMB 4.25 million (from October 31, 2001, to October 30, 2012). The main reasons are:

1. The criminal judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177 of the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin First Intermediate Court) and the criminal judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin Higher People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Higher Court) have been revoked by the criminal judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of the Supreme People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Supreme Court). The review decision of the Ministry of Public Security, citing the already revoked criminal judgments to determine the legality of the recovery act by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, has no valid grounds; even if the recovery of the claimant's property was based on the criminal judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005 of the Tianjin Higher Court, it is also erroneous because that judgment did not determine that the RMB 12.72 million was proceeds of crime and did not order its recovery.

2. The criminal judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of the Supreme Court determined that on the day of each of the claimant's two deposits, she received high interest payments from Zhang Shili and others, and only afterwards did Zhang Shili and others, with the help of Yang Zhaoyuan, the director of the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch of the Tianjin Heping Sub-branch of the Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch), fraudulently obtain the money for their own use. Thus, the high interest paid by Zhang Shili and others to the claimant was unrelated to the proceeds of the bill fraud case. The criminal judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 also determined that the claimant's deposit of RMB 55 million was a lawful deposit, and the claimant was also a victim of the fraud committed by Zhang Shili and others in collusion with internal bank personnel, and she has the right to demand the return of that amount.

3. Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Fraud Cases provides: "Where an actor has used the defrauded property to repay personal debts, pay for goods, or for other economic activities, if the recipient knew that the property was defrauded and received it, it constitutes malicious acquisition and shall be recovered in all cases; if it truly constitutes bona fide acquisition, recovery shall no longer be made." The claimant only received high interest as agreed and was not aware that Zhang Shili and others were committing criminal activities by fraudulent means. Therefore, even if the high interest paid to the claimant by Zhang Shili and others was from the proceeds of crime, since the claimant did not know that the money was obtained by fraud, it should be considered bona fide acquisition, and that amount should not be recovered.

4. The review decision of the Ministry of Public Security, finding that the claimant's act of depositing funds and receiving high interest violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, constitutes an error in the application of law.

The Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau responded to the Compensation Committee of this Court, contending that Ma Ping's claim for the return of RMB 12.72 million and interest is without legal basis. The main reasons are:

1. The RMB 12.72 million was proceeds of crime from the bill fraud case of Zhang Shili and others, and should be recovered and returned as a matter of law. Moreover, the fact that the Economic Crime Investigation General Team of this Bureau recovered and returned the proceeds of crime has been confirmed by the legally effective criminal judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005.

2. Although the criminal judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of the Supreme Court declared that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu did not commit the crime of illegally relending at high interest rates, it simultaneously found that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu did receive high interest, and their conduct violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China. That judgment did not review the act of the public security authority in recovering the proceeds of crime from the bill fraud case of Zhang Shili and others, nor did it address the determination of the recovery of that amount by the public security authority. Therefore, Ma Ping's argument that the Supreme Court judgment proves that her deposit was unrelated to the proceeds of crime in the bill fraud case of Zhang Shili and others and that the recovery act of the public security authority was unlawful cannot stand.

3. During the investigation by the public security authority, Ma Ping voluntarily proposed to turn over the high interest she had received and provided written materials. Ma Ping and Zhang Mu voluntarily cooperated with the work of the public security authority, and the procedures for the transfer of funds were all handled by Zhang Mu on the entrustment of Ma Ping. After the Economic Crime Investigation General Team of this Bureau handled the seizure procedures in accordance with the law, the recovery of that amount and its subsequent return to the victimized entity were in compliance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (1996). Ma Ping's argument that she was coerced into surrendering the money and that the public security authority's recovery was unlawful cannot stand.

The Ministry of Public Security submitted a written opinion to the Compensation Committee of this Court, stating that the criminal compensation review decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi (2012) No. 2) is based on clear facts and correct application of law and should be upheld. The main reasons are:

1. The RMB 12.72 million recovered by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau was proceeds of crime from the bill fraud case of Zhang Shili and others, as established through investigation and confirmed by legally effective court judgments. The criminal judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005 of the Tianjin Higher Court found that "Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. received a total of RMB 12.72 million in high interest paid by Zhang Shili and Xu Guangfa, and that amount has been returned by the public security authority to the defrauded bank." That judgment adopted the basic fact found in the first instance judgment that Zhang Shili and others used part of the defrauded proceeds as high interest payments to Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., affirmed and supported the recovery of that amount by the public security authority, and only corrected the first instance judgment's order to continue recovering RMB 200,000. Although the review decision of this Ministry cited the text of the criminal judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005 and mistakenly listed the case number due to a clerical error, this is a defect in document preparation and does not affect the determination of objective facts or the validity of the conclusion. The recovery by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau of the RMB 12.72 million in proceeds of crime from the bill fraud case of Zhang Shili and others and its return to the defrauded bank complied with the provisions of Article 198 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (1996). Ma Ping's argument that this amount should not be recovered cannot stand.

2. The criminal judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of the Supreme Court found that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu's conduct did not constitute the crime of illegally relending at high interest rates but violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China. Ma Ping deposited funds in the bank but received high interest from Zhang Shili and others, indicating that Ma Ping was not acting in good faith. The payment of high interest to Ma Ping by Zhang Shili and others was part of the implementation of the bill fraud activity, a criminal means to achieve the purpose of fraud, and not a normal economic activity. Therefore, the high interest received by Ma Ping does not fall under the provisions of Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Fraud Cases concerning bona fide acquisition. Ma Ping's argument that the receipt of high interest was bona fide acquisition and should not be recovered cannot stand.

3. There is no evidence to support Ma Ping's claim that she was coerced into surrendering the money by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, or that the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau and the Bank of China colluded to coerce her. On the contrary, existing evidence shows that during questioning by the public security authority, Ma Ping voluntarily offered to surrender the high interest she had received, personally wrote three documents, and entrusted Zhang Mu to handle the procedures on her behalf. Ma Ping's argument that she was coerced into surrendering the money and that the public security authority's recovery was unlawful cannot stand.

The Compensation Committee of this Court, upon trial, finds the following facts:

On November 29, 2000, the Tianjin Heping Sub-branch of the Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Heping Sub-branch) reported to the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau that a fund fraud group was using forged seals to defraud bank funds. The Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau filed the case on the same day. On December 3, 2000, Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others were criminally detained on suspicion of bill fraud. The Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, through investigation, believed that from October 1999 to November 2000, Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others used high interest rates to attract deposits from 17 entities, including Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinwan Company; the company was subsequently renamed Tianjin Zhidi Industrial Development Co., Ltd. and Tianjin Guanbo Industrial Development Co., Ltd., and was dissolved on June 7, 2005), involving more than RMB 140 million. The high interest paid was from the proceeds of crime obtained by Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others through bill fraud. Accordingly, on December 8, 2000, the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau froze the deposit of RMB 55 million in Xinwan Company's account No. 06909708211001 at the Heping Sub-branch. Subsequently, the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, upon further investigation, initiated a criminal investigation against Ma Ping and her husband Zhang Mu (they married on October 28, 1998, and divorced on November 17, 2008) on suspicion of illegally relending at high interest rates, on the basis that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu were the contributors of Xinwan Company.

During the investigation of both cases, the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, based on 58 testimonies from 17 witnesses and the confessions of Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, Ma Ping, and Zhang Mu, concluded that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, in accordance with prior discussions with Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others, deposited RMB 55 million under the name of Xinwan Company at the designated Kaixuanmen Sub-branch and received from Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others a total of 17 high interest payments totaling RMB 12.72 million (deposited at Beijing Commercial Bank, etc.), which were paid from the proceeds of the bill fraud. That amount should be recovered and returned to the defrauded bank. Ma Ping also expressed willingness to return the high interest she had received to the bank and entrusted Zhang Mu to handle the relevant procedures. On October 31, 2001, the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau lifted the freeze on RMB 20 million of the RMB 55 million. On November 2 of the same year, Zhang Mu handled the procedures for transferring RMB 20 million and interest of RMB 397,100 into the account of the Economic Crime Investigation General Team of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau. On November 6 of the same year, the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau returned RMB 12.72 million to the Tianjin Branch of the Bank of China. The remaining RMB 7.6771 million was transferred together with the case of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu for illegally relending at high interest rates to the Tianjin First Intermediate Court, where it was subsequently confiscated by that court. Of the remaining RMB 35 million in account No. 06909708211001, RMB 24.542 million was deducted by the Tianjin Higher Court in connection with the case of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu for illegally relending at high interest rates, and the remaining RMB 10.458 million was deducted by the Beijing Second Intermediate Court in a separate case.

On December 17, 2002, the Tianjin First Intermediate Court issued a criminal judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113 in the case of defendants Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and four others suspected of bill fraud. That judgment found in part the following facts of the crimes of Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and four others: "Between October 1999 and January 2000, defendants Zhang Shuying and Zhang Shili, through Kang Jian, Wang Cheng, and others, induced Tianjin Automobile Industry Sales and Trade Co., Ltd. to deposit RMB 3 million, Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. to deposit RMB 55 million, and defendant Zhang Shili, together with Cui Zheng (already sentenced), induced the Hexi Business Department of the Tianjin Dagang District Plastic and Electrical Factory to deposit RMB 1 million, all at the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch, and opened one-year fixed-term accounts. At the same time, defendant Zhang Shili obtained from Yang Zhaoyuan (separately handled), the director of that sub-branch, the bank's reserved seal card, copies of business licenses, and fixed-term deposit confirmation certificates for the above two companies. Using privately engraved official seals, financial seals, and personal name seals of those units, and fabricating false industrial and mineral product purchase and sale contracts, they pledged the deposit confirmation certificates, and using the names of Tianjin Zhongchao Trade Co., Ltd., Tianjin Zhongyun Industrial Co., Ltd., and Tianjin Development Zone Shicheng Development Co., Ltd., they issued bank acceptance bills totaling RMB 59 million, paying discount interest of RMB 3,067,350.49, and withdrawing RMB 55,432,649.51. After paying high interest of RMB 352,500 to Tianjin Automobile Industry Sales and Trade Co., Ltd. (RMB 5,000 recovered by the public security authority), and high interest of RMB 12.92 million to Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (RMB 12.72 million recovered by the public security authority), defendant Zhang Shuying actually received proceeds of crime in the amount of RMB 1.2875 million; defendant Xu Guangfa actually received proceeds of crime in the amount of RMB 20,193,824.755; and defendant Zhang Shili actually received proceeds of crime in the amount of RMB 20,678,824.755." The judgment also found: "After the case was uncovered, the public security authority sealed and seized...; recovered property valued at RMB 17,702,759.54 from Zhang Shuying...; recovered high interest paid by the defendants totaling RMB 19,374,998.6. The above recovered items and premises have been appraised by the public security authority and, together with the recovered proceeds of crime, returned to the defrauded unit." Accordingly, the judgment ordered: Zhang Shuying and Zhang Shili were convicted of bill fraud and sentenced to life imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for life and confiscation of all personal property...; the proceeds of crime obtained by each defendant shall continue to be recovered and, together with other recovered proceeds of crime, returned to the respective defrauded units in accordance with the law.

Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and the four other defendants appealed. On July 23, 2003, the Tianjin Higher Court issued a criminal judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005, which affirmed and summarized the main facts found in the criminal judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113, and found that the value of the property recovered from each appellant after the case was uncovered was as follows: "...the high interest paid by the appellants totaling RMB 19,374,999 was recovered, and property valued at RMB 76,053 was recovered from the separately handled defendant Cui Zheng. The above recovered property has been returned by the public security authority to the relevant defrauded banks." Based on the facts, the judgment found that Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and the four others, in order to obtain huge sums of funds, individually or jointly, used high interest as a lure to attract deposits to their designated banks, fraudulently opened bank acceptance bills or directly transferred funds by check, illegally appropriating the funds for themselves. Their acts constituted the crime of bill fraud, with an especially large amount of crime and causing particularly significant economic losses to the state. The judgment held: "Regarding the first instance court's order to continue recovering RMB 200,000 from Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Upon examination, Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. received a total of RMB 12.72 million in high interest paid by Zhang Shili and Xu Guangfa, and that amount has been returned by the public security authority to the defrauded bank. The first instance judgment's order to continue recovering RMB 200,000 from Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. was erroneous and should be corrected." Accordingly, the judgment ordered: 1. The conviction and sentencing of defendants Zhang Shuying and Zhang Shili, and the conviction of defendants Liu Jiali and Xu Guangfa in item 1 of the criminal judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113 were affirmed...; items 3 to 15 of the list of recovered proceeds of crime in item 2 were affirmed...; 2. The sentencing of defendants Liu Jiali and Xu Guangfa in item 1 of the criminal judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113 was vacated; the orders in item 2 for continued recovery from Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and Liu Jiali were vacated...; items 1, 2, and 16 of the list of recovered proceeds of crime, namely, RMB 767,500 from Tianjin Automobile Industry Sales and Trade Co., Ltd., RMB 200,000 from Tianjin Xinwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and property from Liu Jiali's business, Tianjin Jialida Chemical Dye Co., Ltd., were vacated... The criminal judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005 has become legally effective.

Further facts found: On April 30, 2002, the Tianjin First Intermediate Court issued a criminal judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177 in the case of Ma Ping and Zhang Mu suspected of illegally relending at high interest rates, convicting Ma Ping of the crime of illegally relending at high interest rates, sentencing her to six years' imprisonment, a fine of RMB 22.84 million, and expulsion; convicting Zhang Mu of the same crime, sentencing him to three years' imprisonment, a fine of RMB 18.27 million; and ordering the confiscation of illegal gains of RMB 4.5684 million.

Ma Ping and Zhang Mu appealed that judgment. On April 14, 2004, the Tianjin Higher Court issued a criminal judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089, convicting Ma Ping of the crime of illegally relending at high interest rates, sentencing her to six years' imprisonment, a fine of RMB 19 million, and expulsion; convicting Zhang Mu of the same crime, sentencing him to three years' imprisonment, suspended for three years, and a fine of RMB 15.2 million; and ordering the confiscation of illegal gains of RMB 679,500, to be turned over to the state treasury.

Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, still dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, filed a petition. On December 14, 2007, this Court issued a criminal judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1, holding: Ma Ping and Zhang Mu deposited RMB 55 million at the Kaixuanmen Sub-branch, including RMB 30.2 million in bank loans, and the deposit procedures were lawful. A deposit relationship was formed between Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, as depositors, and the bank. Zhang Shili and Xu Guangfa, using the deposit confirmation certificates for the above amount provided by Yang Zhaoyuan, forged the relevant seals and Zhang Mu's chop, and fraudulently obtained bank credit funds. It cannot be proven that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu's conduct constituted a relending activity. Ma Ping and Zhang Mu's conduct violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China but did not constitute a crime. Accordingly, the judgment vacated the criminal judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 177 of the Tianjin First Intermediate Court and the criminal judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin Higher Court, and acquitted Ma Ping and Zhang Mu.

It was further found that after the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court became effective, Ma Ping submitted to the Tianjin High People's Court an application signed by Ma Ping, Zhang Mu, and Ma Junchen (Ma Ping's father, former legal representative and shareholder of Xinwan Company), a declaration issued by the shareholders of Xinwan Company stating that the funds in the company's account were Ma Ping's own funds, deposited in the name of Xinwan Company by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, and did not belong to Xinwan Company, a power of attorney, and certificates of the marital relationship between Ma Ping and Zhang Mu, among other materials, applying for the return of the involved funds of RMB 32,219,100. On November 11 and 13, 2008, the Tianjin High People's Court returned RMB 32,219,100 (including interest of RMB 397,100) out of the relevant funds in the account of Xinwan Company that had been frozen by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau and transferred with the case to the account designated by Ma Ping.

On December 13, 2011, Ma Ping applied to the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau for state compensation on the ground of wrongful recovery by the Bureau. On February 7, 2012, the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau issued the Criminal Compensation Decision (Jin Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 001), holding that: the recovery, freezing, and return of the involved RMB 12,720,000 by its Economic Crime Investigation Division constituted stolen funds in the case of Zhang Shuying's bill fraud; the Bureau's lawful recovery complied with legal provisions; the other funds had been transferred with the case to the prosecutorial and judicial authorities for decision by the court, and were unrelated to the Bureau; the investigators of the Bureau strictly handled the case according to law and should not be held legally liable. Accordingly, it decided that Ma Ping should not be compensated.

On February 24, 2012, Ma Ping applied to the Ministry of Public Security for reconsideration of the compensation. On April 19, 2012, the Ministry of Public Security issued the Criminal Compensation Reconsideration Decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 2), holding that: the Criminal Judgment (2002) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 089 of the Tianjin High People's Court had already determined that the RMB 12,720,000 recovered by the public security organs were stolen funds in the case of bill fraud by Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others. Since money is a fungible thing, the public security organs' recovery of stolen funds from the deposit account complied with legal provisions. Ma Ping's claim that the RMB 12,720,000 returned to the bank were lawful deposits unrelated to the bill fraud case of Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others could not be established. The Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of the Supreme People's Court determined that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu's act of storing funds to obtain high interest did not constitute a crime, but also pointed out that their act violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China. It did not review the recovery of funds by the public security organs and did not address the determination of the RMB 12,720,000 recovered by the public security organs. Ma Ping's claim that the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of the Supreme People's Court proved that her deposit was unrelated to the stolen funds in the bill fraud case of Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others could not be established. During interrogation by the public security organs, Ma Ping voluntarily offered to hand over the high interest she had received, wrote three documents, and entrusted Zhang Mu to handle the matter. The Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau lawfully handled the seizure procedures, recovered the money, and returned it to the victim, which complied with the provisions of Article 198 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (1996). Ma Ping's claim of being coerced to pay and the public security organs' unlawful recovery could not be established. Ma Ping's act of storing funds to collect high interest violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, was inherently illegal, and did not constitute bona fide acquisition. The high interest of RMB 12,720,000 paid by Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others to Ma Ping was part of the implementation of the bill fraud activity, a criminal means to achieve the fraudulent purpose, not a normal economic activity. Ma Ping deposited funds in the bank but received high interest of up to RMB 12,720,000 from Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others, indicating that Ma Ping was not acting in good faith. Ma Ping's claim that receiving high interest constituted bona fide acquisition and that the case-handling department should return it could not be established. Accordingly, it was decided to uphold the Criminal Compensation Decision (Jin Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 001) of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau.

The above facts are confirmed by documents including the Criminal Judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113 of the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court, the Criminal Judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005 of the Tianjin High People's Court, the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court, the Criminal Compensation Decision (Jin Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 001) of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, and the Criminal Compensation Reconsideration Decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 2) of the Ministry of Public Security.

The Compensation Committee of this Court is of the opinion that, according to the determination in the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court, Ma Ping and Zhang Mu deposited funds in the name of Xinwan Company. The declaration of the shareholders of Xinwan Company also confirms that the funds in the account of Xinwan Company frozen by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau were Ma Ping's own funds, deposited by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu in the name of Xinwan Company, and did not belong to Xinwan Company. Ma Ping, as the actual contributor of the company, is entitled to claim rights over the RMB 12,720,000 recovered and returned to the bank by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau in accordance with the law.

Based on the opinions of all parties, the focus of the dispute in this case is summarized as: whether the act of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau in recovering and returning RMB 12,720,000 to the bank constitutes an illegal infringement as stipulated in Article 18(1) of the State Compensation Law; whether Ma Ping's act of receiving high interest constitutes bona fide acquisition; and whether Ma Ping's act violates the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China. Based on the above facts, the Compensation Committee of this Court makes the following determinations:

1. The act of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau in recovering RMB 12,720,000 as stolen funds and returning them to the bank was made in accordance with the provisions of Article 198 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (1996) and has been confirmed by an effective criminal judgment of the People's Court. This act is lawful and well-founded, and does not constitute the illegal infringement situation stipulated in Article 18(1) of the State Compensation Law.

Article 198 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (1996) provides that public security organs, People's Procuratorates, and People's Courts shall properly keep the property and its fruits seized or frozen from criminal suspects or defendants for verification. No unit or individual may misappropriate or dispose of them without authorization. The lawful property of victims shall be returned in a timely manner.

According to the facts found by the Criminal Judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113 of the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court and the Criminal Judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005 of the Tianjin High People's Court, the defendants Zhang Shuying and Zhang Shili induced RMB 55,000,000 of Xinwan Company to be deposited at Kaixuanmen Sub-branch Office and paid high interest of RMB 12,720,000 to Xinwan Company, then fraudulently opened bank acceptance bills to take the RMB 55,000,000 for themselves. Their crime of bill fraud was established and confirmed by an effective criminal judgment. The high interest of RMB 12,720,000 received by Xinwan Company was the consideration paid by Zhang Shuying, Zhang Shili, and others for illegally attracting deposits at high interest to commit bill fraud, and in nature it constitutes part of the fraudulently obtained stolen funds. The Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau, in accordance with Article 198 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (1996), recovered the high interest of RMB 12,720,000 received by Xinwan Company and returned it to the victim, which was lawful and well-founded, and has been confirmed by an effective criminal judgment of the People's Court.

The Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court was a review of whether the crime of relending at high interest by Ma Ping and Zhang Mu was established. That judgment determined that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu deposited RMB 55,000,000 at Kaixuanmen Sub-branch Office, including RMB 30,200,000 from bank loans; the deposit procedures handled were lawful, and a deposit relationship was formed between them as depositors and the bank. Zhang Shili and others used the deposit certificate of the above funds provided by Yang Zhaoyuan to forge relevant seals and Zhang Mu's seal to defraud bank credit funds, which could not prove that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu's act constituted relending. That judgment did not review the recovery of RMB 12,720,000 by the public security organs; the facts related to the recovery were reviewed and determined by the effective criminal judgment in the bill fraud case of Zhang Shili and others. Therefore, although the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court determined that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu did not constitute the crime of relending at high interest, it does not affect the determination in the previous effective criminal judgment that the high interest of RMB 12,720,000 paid by Zhang Shili and others to Ma Ping and Zhang Mu was stolen funds in the bill fraud case, nor does it affect the validity of the confirmation by the effective criminal judgment of the act of the public security organs in recovering stolen funds and returning them to the victim.

Regarding the recovery and deduction of RMB 12,720,000 from the lawful deposit account of RMB 55,000,000. Since the RMB 12,720,000 was recovered in the name of stolen funds, even if lawfully deposited in the bank, its inherent illegality cannot be negated. Because money is a fungible thing and has the nature of equivalent exchange, after Ma Ping received the high interest illegally paid by Zhang Shili and others, she had deposited the high interest into other accounts. Therefore, whether recovering and deducting the stolen funds of RMB 12,720,000 from the RMB 55,000,000 deposit account or from other accounts of Ma Ping makes no essential difference. Relevant evidence also confirms that the deduction of the high interest of RMB 12,720,000 from the RMB 55,000,000 deposit account was handled by Ma Ping writing three documents and entrusting Zhang Mu to cooperate with the public security organs. In view of this, the act of the public security organs in recovering and deducting the stolen funds of RMB 12,720,000 from the RMB 55,000,000 deposit account and returning them to the victim was not improper.

The reconsideration decision of the Ministry of Public Security cited relevant expressions from the Criminal Judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 113 and the Criminal Judgment (2003) Jin Gao Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 005. Although there was a typographical error in the document number, this is a defect in document preparation and does not affect the determination of objective facts and the establishment of the conclusion in the reconsideration decision.

In summary, Ma Ping's claim that the recovery and return by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau lacked legal and judgment basis and should be found unlawful cannot be established.

2. Ma Ping's act of receiving high interest of RMB 12,720,000 paid by Zhang Shili and others with stolen funds does not meet the circumstances of bona fide acquisition stipulated in Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Fraud Cases.

Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Fraud Cases provides: "If the actor has used the fraudulently obtained property to repay personal debts, payments for goods, or other economic activities, if the other party knowingly receives the fraudulently obtained property, it constitutes malicious acquisition and shall be recovered in all cases; if it is indeed bona fide acquisition, it shall no longer be recovered." An important prerequisite for applying this provision is that the actor has used the fraudulently obtained property for repaying personal debts, payments for goods, or other economic activities, i.e., the use should be for lawful interests. Only under this prerequisite is it necessary to further examine whether the recipient is bona fide. If the use of the property received by the recipient is lawful and the recipient did not know it was fraudulently obtained property, it should be deemed bona fide acquisition; if the use of the property received is unlawful, even if the recipient did not know it was fraudulently obtained property, it should be recovered, and the above interpretation regarding bona fide acquisition does not apply.

In this case, Ma Ping, upon an offer of high-interest deposit attraction, deposited RMB 55,000,000 at Kaixuanmen Sub-branch Office, forming a deposit contract legal relationship with the bank, which was also confirmed by the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court. If she needed to legally relend to a third party or entrust with financial management, she would have to sign a relevant entrusted loan agreement or financial management agreement with the bank. The facts of this case show that Ma Ping did not sign any relevant agreement with the bank, so there was no other lawful legal relationship between her and the bank or a third party outside the deposit contract legal relationship. Under these circumstances, her receipt of high interest paid by Zhang Shili and others had no legal basis. Moreover, the reason Ma Ping and Zhang Shili and others did not choose direct lending but used the bank as an intermediary for fund use was that they intended to use the bank for fund lending, a practice to avoid risks for both parties and shift the risk to the bank, which is illegal. Therefore, the high interest obtained by Ma Ping is not a lawful interest protected by law and does not meet the prerequisite for applying Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Fraud Cases. Even if Ma Ping could prove that she did not know the high interest was paid with fraudulently obtained stolen funds, it does not constitute bona fide acquisition under this judicial interpretation. Therefore, Ma Ping's claim that her receipt of high interest constituted bona fide acquisition and should not be recovered cannot be established.

3. Whether Ma Ping's act violates the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China is not within the scope of review in state compensation cases.

Ma Ping argued that the Criminal Judgment of this Court determined that she violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, and that the reconsideration decision of the Ministry of Public Security cited this determination, which constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected. The Compensation Committee of this Court is of the opinion that the Criminal Judgment (2006) Xing Ti Zi No. 1 of this Court's determination that Ma Ping and Zhang Mu's receipt of high interest violated the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China is not improper. Article 31 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Commercial banks shall determine the deposit interest rates within the upper and lower limits of the deposit interest rates prescribed by the People's Bank of China and shall announce them." This is a norm for the conduct of commercial banks and also a norm for the financial order, and has a reflexive binding effect on transaction counterparties who have deposit relationships with commercial banks. Since this determination was made by an effective criminal judgment, it is not within the scope of review in state compensation cases. If Ma Ping has objections to this, she should seek resolution through other channels.

In summary, the act of the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau in recovering and returning RMB 12,720,000 does not constitute the illegal infringement situation stipulated in Article 18(1) of the State Compensation Law. The matters and reasons raised by Ma Ping in her application lack legal basis and should not be supported. The Criminal Compensation Reconsideration Decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 2) of the Ministry of Public Security has clear factual findings and correct application of law. Although there is a typographical error in a specific document number, it does not affect the determination of objective facts and the establishment of the conclusion in the decision, and therefore it should be upheld. Pursuant to Article 18(1), Article 25(2), and Article 29 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 2 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 19(1) and Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Procedures for the Compensation Committee of the People's Court to Hear State Compensation Cases, after deliberation by the Judicial Committee of this Court, the decision is as follows:

Uphold the Criminal Compensation Reconsideration Decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 2) of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China.

This decision is a legally effective decision.
